summary:
I confirmed R5-A, R5-B and R5-C with the reviewer's repro, ported to servd_test_money_fu, and fixed all three. R6-A was already fixed in the working tree, so it needed no change.

All three R5 bugs come from one cause. On a cancelled ticket, the hand-back was booked as if every receipt had been held as a refund due in 1110. That is only true for a drawer that closes after the cancel. Anything posted before the cancel was never undone:
- a close that booked a non-till order's cash as non-till cash (Dr 1015 / Cr 1010)
- a home drawer's close that booked a till sale
- a void refund booked as a sale refund while the order was open

The fix is in `backend/src/modules/pos/service.ts`, in the refund area only. The hand-back on a cancelled ticket no longer goes through `postRefundPayment`'s cancelled branch. `writeRefundTx` gets an optional `post` hook, and `refundDueOnCancelledTicket` books through a new `bookCancelledHandBackTx`, in the same order-locked transaction. It does two things:

1. **Unwind, once per order** (`order.cancel_unwind:<orderId>`, idempotent). For every drawer whose close was posted before the cancel (no REFUND DUE line naming the order), it works out what that close booked for the ticket. It does this by re-running the close's own formula (`summariseShiftSales`) on the order alone, so no second sale formula exists. It then reverses revenue, 4100, 2095, tax (to the account the sale credited, via `refundTaxAccountFor`), 7010, 2050, 2080 (skipped for a pre-ONL-05 sale), 7030 and 8010 rounding. It also reverses the non-money lines of the order's earlier `order.refund` entries (the sale-refund shares). The balance goes to where the money is owed from: 1010 or 1030 up to what a pre-cancel close left there for a non-till ticket, and the rest to 1110.
2. **Each hand-back** (`order.refund:<id>`, so the shift close still skips it) debits where its tender's money sits. That is 1010 for cash, or 1030 for card a close never booked, up to what is left there, and 1110 for the rest. It credits the drawer, or 1030 for card. The simple case (every receipt on a drawer that closes after the cancel) is unchanged: the same two-line Dr 1110 / Cr 1015 entry, with no unwind.

Result: once the ticket is fully handed back, revenue, GST, 4100, 2095, 1110, 1010 and the tender accounts all net to zero for it, whatever order the close, void, cancel and hand-back happened in.

I also added `postCancelledTicketUnwind(orderId)` for the cancel path. It takes the order lock, is idempotent, returns null when there is nothing to undo, and refuses NOT_CANCELLED (422) for an order that is not cancelled.

R6-A: `reports/service.ts` `salesBuckets` already has `legacyCardSaleCheck`, which uses the same check as `saleBookingOf.legacyGiftCard`. It skips the gift-card add-back for a pre-ONL-05 sale and values that sale's refunds and card restores without the card. The existing R6-A test (gross 650 / net 500, register = ledger after a partial and a full refund) passes. I did not rewrite it.

Rejected: none of the four findings. R6-A is real but was already addressed.

The seed scripts (`seed-live-state.ts`, `seed-customer-experience.ts`) don't touch refunds or cancels, so I left them alone. `giftCards/service.ts` and `pos/routes.ts` needed no change; the existing error handler already maps the new NOT_CANCELLED code.

items.note: Reproduced: an online cash order that closed as non-till cash and was then cancelled left 1110 Dr 11,500 and 1010 Cr 11,500. Now the hand-back books Dr 1010 / Cr 1015. Card a pre-cancel close never booked goes back as Dr 1030 / Cr 1030. Tested: two cases, all accounts net to zero.

Reproduced: 1110 left Cr 2,300, revenue Dr 2,000, tax Dr 300. Now the first hand-back posts the unwind once (Cr 4090 2,000 / Cr 2030 300 / Dr 1110 2,300; Dr 1010 instead when the drawer had closed before the cancel). Tested: a split hand-back where the unwind posts once, and the combined R5-A + R5-B case. Gap: when the whole amount was refunded before the cancel there is no hand-back to trigger the unwind; `postCancelledTicketUnwind` covers it (tested) but is not wired into the cancel path yet.

Reproduced: revenue 5,652, GST 848 and 1110 Dr 6,500 were left after the hand-back. Now the unwind reverses the sale the home drawer booked, through the close's own formula (Dr 4090 10,000 / Dr 2030 1,500 / Cr 1110 11,500), and the hand-back is Dr 1110 / Cr 1015, never a sale refund. Tested, including service charge, tip, and a card on a second drawer that closes after the cancel. Same gap as R5-B for a booked-then-cancelled till bill that took no money.

Already fixed in the working tree before this pass: `legacyCardSaleCheck` in `salesBuckets` skips the add-back and values refunds and card restores without the card when there is no 2080 debit naming the order. Covered by the existing R6-A test, which passes.

tests:
`npx tsc --noEmit -p .` in backend passes.

`tests/auditMoneyFollowups.test.ts`: 21/21 pass, including 7 new R5-A/B/C tests. With the fix's `post:` hook commented out, 6 of the 7 new tests fail, so they catch the bug. The 7th calls `postCancelledTicketUnwind` directly, so it passes either way.

17 related suites pass, 214 tests: auditLedgerFollowups, auditLedgerSales, auditLedgerLoyalty, auditOrdersRefund, auditTillMoney, auditTillReview, auditTillShift, auditTillGiftCard, auditSplit, cashDrawer, terminalRefund, auditReports, reports, booksLedger, orderLifecycle, auditOrdersFollowup, sepFinance.

The reviewer's scratchpad repro, run against servd_test_money_fu: scenario 2 (R5-A) now passes. Scenario 1 still fails its own assertion, and scenario 3 still prints non-zero totals. That is only because the repro does not include the new `order.cancel_unwind:<orderId>` entry in the lines it adds up. With that entry included, 1110, revenue and GST net to zero, as asserted in the new tests.
needsOtherFiles:
1. orders/* (cancel path, owned by another agent): after a cancel or reject commits, call `postCancelledTicketUnwind(orderId)` from `pos/service.ts` (idempotent). Without that call, two cases keep wrong books: a ticket refunded in full before the cancel (R5-B), and a till bill whose home drawer booked the sale but which took no money (R5-C). Neither has a hand-back to trigger the unwind.
2. accounting/orderPosting.ts `postRefundPayment` (cancelled branch) still has the old 1110-only logic. Nothing in the refund engine uses it for cancelled tickets any more, but a future caller or backfill would repeat R5-A. It should either delegate to the same logic or refuse cancelled orders. Ideally the unwind and hand-back helpers move into accounting/ so there is one owner.
3. Known limits:
   - The unwind re-derives a pre-cancel close from the order's current figures, so an order edited between that close and the cancel would be unwound on the new figures.
   - Race: if a shift close posting reads the order as live while the cancel is committing, and the unwind is posted before that close entry exists, the close's sale booking is not unwound.
